title: Closed-loop learning links donor–acceptor molecules’ photostability to higher triplet states
summary: A closed-loop synthesis and learning campaign found that solution photostability across a donor–bridge–acceptor molecular series correlated with the high-energy portion of the triplet excited-state manifold, beyond the commonly considered lowest triplet state. Researchers tested the model-derived hypothesis on an experimental set and changed solvent triplet energy to test the proposed Dexter triplet-energy-transfer degradation pathway. The study used Bayesian optimization and interpretable supervised learning to extract the chemical hypothesis from measured photostability data.
ai_technology: Closed-loop transfer (CLT), combining Gryffin Bayesian optimization with physics-feature supervised learning
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; University of Toronto; Vector Institute; University of Chicago; University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: Researchers tested the model-derived hypothesis on an experimental set and changed solvent triplet energy to test the proposed Dexter triplet-energy-transfer degradation pathway.
evidence.unknown: The finding concerns solution photostability in the studied donor–bridge–acceptor chemical space; it does not by itself establish a universal law for all organic molecules or performance in processed films/devices. The work used human expertise in the loop and experimentally tested the model-generated hypothesis. Device deployment was not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization recommended molecules for automated modular synthesis and photostability assays; an interpretable supervised model using physics-based features identified a triplet-state hypothesis, which researchers tested with experimental test sets and solvent-energy perturbation. AI guided experimental selection and surfaced a specific chemical relationship; the follow-up measurements tested it.
